components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Command-gradient action button for primary workflow moves.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; height: 36px; padding: 0 14px; border-radius: 8px; border: 1px solid rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.08); background: linear-gradient(97deg, #455eb5 9%, #5643cc 44%, #673fd7 65%); color: #f7f8f8; font-family: Inter, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 500; letter-spacing: 0; box-shadow: inset 0 1px 0 rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.22), 0 8px 18px rgba(47, 35, 120, 0.22); transition: filter 150ms cubic-bezier(0.2, 0.9, 0.2, 1), box-shadow 150ms cubic-bezier(0.2, 0.9, 0.2, 1); } .ds-btn-primary:hover { filter: brightness(1.1); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 1px rgba(103, 63, 215, 0.55), 0 0 0 4px rgba(103, 63, 215, 0.13); }

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: Low-emphasis action button for secondary controls and safe alternatives.
components.css: .ds-btn-secondary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; height: 36px; padding: 0 14px; border-radius: 8px; border: 1px solid rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.10); background: rgba(247, 248, 248, 0.06); color: #f7f8f8; font-family: Inter, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 500; letter-spacing: 0; transition: background 150ms cubic-bezier(0.2, 0.9, 0.2, 1), border-color 150ms cubic-bezier(0.2, 0.9, 0.2, 1); } .ds-btn-secondary:hover { border-color: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.16); background: rgba(247, 248, 248, 0.09); } .ds-btn-secondary:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 1px rgba(103, 63, 215, 0.55), 0 0 0 4px rgba(103, 63, 215, 0.13); }

components.name: Status Badge

components.name: Input Shell
components.description: Embedded search or command field for cached mail and palette entry.
components.css: .ds-input-shell { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 10px; height: 36px; padding: 0 12px; border-radius: 8px; border: 1px solid rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.10); background: rgba(32, 36, 56, 0.34); box-shadow: 0 1px 0 rgba(247, 248, 248, 0.03) inset; color: #b4bcd0; font-family: Inter, sans-serif; font-size: 13px; letter-spacing: 0; } .ds-input-shell input { width: 100%; border: 0; outline: 0; background: transparent; color: #f7f8f8; font: inherit; } .ds-input-shell input::placeholder { color: #b4bcd0; } .ds-input-shell:focus-within { box-shadow: 0 0 0 1px rgba(103, 63, 215, 0.55), 0 0 0 4px rgba(103, 63, 215, 0.13); }

components.name: Thread Row Selected
components.description: Selected mailbox row with accent wash, inset command marker, and dense message metadata.
components.css: .ds-thread-row { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 1fr auto; gap: 6px 12px; width: 100%; padding: 10px 12px; border-radius: 8px; border: 1px solid rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.12); background: linear-gradient(90deg, rgba(69, 94, 181, 0.18), transparent 68%), rgba(32, 36, 56, 0.50); box-shadow: inset 2px 0 0 #673fd7; color: #f7f8f8; font-family: Inter, sans-serif; text-align: left; letter-spacing: 0; } .ds-thread-row strong { grid-column: 1 / -1; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 500; } .ds-thread-row p { grid-column: 1 / -1; margin: 0; color: #b4bcd0; font-size: 14px; line-height: 1.45; } .ds-thread-from { min-width: 0; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis; white-space: nowrap; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 500; } .ds-thread-time { color: #b4bcd0; font-size: 11px; text-transform: uppercase; }

narrative.overview: HyperMail is a dense desktop control surface for people who operate from their inbox. The interface should feel like a quiet flight deck: dark enough for long sessions, bright enough to read at speed, and structured enough that every status signal has a place. The system uses a restrained dark palette, compact Inter typography, tight radius values, and layered panels to separate navigation, thread work, and context without turning the app into a pile of cards.
keyCharacteristics: Dense but calm desktop information architecture.
Keyboard-first actions with visible shortcut affordances.
Local-first trust signals for offline, queue, sync, and provider state.
Restrained dark theme with violet-blue command emphasis.
Flat tonal layering first, ambient shadow only for shell and command focus.

rules.name: The Command Accent Rule
rules.body: Violet is reserved for focus, selected state, primary action, and AI affordance. If every panel uses violet, nothing is important.

rules.name: The Status Color Rule
rules.body: Green, amber, red, blue, pink, and AI violet belong to mailbox or runtime semantics. Do not use them as arbitrary decoration.

rules.name: The Dense Type Rule
rules.body: Product chrome stays in the 11px to 15px range unless a screen is onboarding or authentication. Do not use hero-scale type inside the mail shell.

rules.name: The No Letterspacing Rule
rules.body: Letter spacing is zero by default. Avoid stretched uppercase labels unless the surrounding UI already uses that exact pattern.

rules.name: The Tonal Layer Rule
rules.body: Prefer panel tint and 1px alpha borders before adding shadow. If a row needs depth, it probably needs clearer hierarchy instead.

rules.name: The Blur Discipline Rule
rules.body: Backdrop blur is allowed for the app frame, command surface, and existing panel primitives. Do not introduce decorative glass cards.

dos: Do use the existing `--hm-*` CSS variables and Tailwind token aliases before introducing new visual values.
Do keep product shell typography compact and scannable.
Do make queue, sync, offline, provider, and AI status visible when those states affect user trust.
Do use semantic status colors only for actual mailbox or runtime meaning.
Do preserve keyboard affordances with visible shortcut hints and focus states.
donts: Don't use generic SaaS hero UI with oversized marketing claims, decorative stat blocks, or productivity cliches.
Don't create decorative card-heavy layouts where every concept is framed inside another box.
Don't use glassmorphism as a default aesthetic. Blur must support shell depth or command focus.
Don't add noisy consumer-mail chrome, playful gradients, social feed patterns, or advertising-style hierarchy.
Don't use vague AI-assistant aesthetics where sparkles and purple glow replace clear workflow value.
Don't hide queue, sync, offline, provider, or AI state when it affects user trust.
Don't use `border-left` or `border-right` wider than 1px as a decorative stripe on cards, rows, callouts, or alerts.
